claims.text: Conventionally processed single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a compositionally matched derivative has coarse grains and coercivity at or below 100 Oe.
High-pressure torsion of single-phase fcc FeCoNi will refine its grain structure into the nanocrystalline regime.
High-pressure torsion can reduce the grain size without altering the alloy's overall composition.
Room-temperature severe plastic deformation is intended to produce grain sizes below 100 nm.
The intervention will produce a high density of grain boundaries.
The intervention will produce a high density of dislocations.
Grain boundaries and dislocations generated by deformation will act as magnetic-domain-wall pinning sites.
The increased defect density will increase magnetic anisotropy.
Domain-wall pinning and increased anisotropy will increase coercivity.
The coercive field may increase by approximately an order of magnitude relative to a baseline at or below 100 Oe.
The coercivity increase will occur without significant loss of saturation magnetization.
The magnitude of coercivity enhancement will depend on the achieved grain refinement and defect density.
The proposed effect is restricted to single-phase fcc FeCoNi processed by severe plastic deformation and measured at room temperature.

contradictions.description: The initial-state and baseline fields allow a compositionally matched high-entropy derivative, whereas the boundary restricts the hypothesis to single-phase fcc FeCoNi and says that compositional modifications are not addressed.
